review.alternative: Entropy production bounds derived via trajectory-level observables or non-conservative force variances may be loose or limited to specific overdamped Langevin or Markovian settings.
review.would_change_mind: Demonstration that non-conservative driving variance fails to bound dissipation in underdamped or strongly coupled non-Markovian dynamics.

claims.statement: Steady-state entropy production rate in overdamped Langevin dynamics can be upper-bounded using only the statistics of driven particles or the variance of the non-conservative force.

support.explanation: Demonstrates upper bounds on entropy production rate in overdamped Langevin systems driven by non-conservative forces using driven particle statistics.
support.passage: For particles in a thermal environment and driven by non-conservative forces, we show that the entropy production rate can be upper bounded by considering only the statistics of the driven particles.

review.alternative: Estimating entropy production from spatiotemporal correlation observables without full distribution reconstruction may severely underestimate total dissipation in systems with hidden microscopic degrees of freedom.
review.would_change_mind: Proof or numerical counterexample where convex duality over sampled trajectory observables yields divergent or uninformative bounds compared to true dissipation.

claims.statement: Trajectory-level entropy production and lower bounds on average dissipation can be inferred from trajectory observables such as spatiotemporal correlations using convex duality without reconstructing full probability distributions.

support.explanation: Shows inference of entropy production lower bounds from trajectory observable samples without reconstructing high-dimensional rate matrices or probability distributions.
support.passage: We infer trajectory-level EP and lower bounds on average EP by exploiting a nonequilibrium analogue of the Maximum Entropy principle, along with convex duality. Our approach uses only samples of trajectory observables, such as spatiotemporal correlations.

actions.findings:
Steady-state entropy production rate in overdamped Langevin dynamics can be upper-bounded using only the statistics of driven particles or the variance of the non-conservative force. [source-05114bb77dcc47b7]

Trajectory-level entropy production and lower bounds on average dissipation can be inferred from trajectory observables such as spatiotemporal correlations using convex duality without reconstructing full probability distributions. [source-dc0bb1a28c9b4193]
actions.limitations: The bounds rely on overdamped Langevin formulations or trajectory-level observable sampling and convex duality; they do not explicitly account for non-Markovian memory overhead or experimental finite-precision noise.
actions.next_questions: How do memory retrieval noise and finite relaxation times alter the tightness of convex-duality-based trajectory entropy production bounds?
